analyzed_vuln.description: The slow-shutdown cleanup has an off-by-one boundary error in its reverse walks of request-added tables. `EG(persistent_functions_count)` is initialized to the function table's pre-request `nNumUsed`, so the first request-added function is stored at bucket index exactly equal to that count. However, the cleanup loop at lines 378-385 breaks when `_idx == EG(persistent_functions_count)` before destroying/removing that bucket. For this PoV, a compiled closure/function `zend_op_array` is therefore left referenced by `EG(function_table)`. `shutdown_compiler()` subsequently destroys `CG(arena)`, freeing that op array. On the following fuzzer request, `shutdown_executor()` iterates the retained table entry at lines 283-285 and reads `op_array->type`, causing the reported heap-use-after-free. The analogous equality checks exist for constants/classes, but this crash specifically follows the stale function-table entry.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: The parser input must compile at least one request-local function/closure far enough for `zend_begin_func_decl()` to insert its arena-backed `zend_op_array` into `CG(function_table)`; the PoV's many anonymous functions provide this. Shutdown must take the non-fast path (`fast_shutdown == false`, as in the sanitizer/tracked-allocation configuration). During the first request shutdown, later request functions may be removed, but the first one at index `persistent_functions_count` is skipped; then `shutdown_compiler()` frees the compiler arena. A subsequent fuzz iteration/request—even the zero-length rerun shown by libFuzzer leak detection—reuses the global function table, and its shutdown dereferences the stale op-array pointer.

args: Please analyze the slow-shutdown reverse cleanup loops in php-src/Zend/zend_execute_API.c lines 365-393. Given that init_executor records each persistent count as the corresponding HashTable nNumUsed before request-local entries are inserted, what exact boundary condition should each reverse iterator use so all request-local entries are deleted but pre-request persistent entries are retained? Also, is php-src/Zend/zend_execute_API.c an ordinary engine source file or part of a fuzzing harness, and are there equivalent cleanup definitions elsewhere under php-src that legitimately should be changed?

The ASan report shows a second-request heap-use-after-free in shutdown_executor at php-src/Zend/zend_execute_API.c:285. On the first request, the slow cleanup loops break when `_idx == EG(persistent_functions_count)`, leaving the first request-added function at that exact bucket index. shutdown_compiler later destroys CG(arena), and the retained function-table pointer is dereferenced during the next shutdown. The constants and classes loops have analogous equality checks. I attempted to patch all three checks from equality to `_idx < persistent_*_count`, because request-local bucket indices begin at the saved nNumUsed count, but the editing tool unexpectedly classified php-src/Zend/zend_execute_API.c as a fuzzer harness and refused the patch. The actual named harness is php-src/sapi/fuzzer/fuzzer-parser.c, which I have not attempted to modify. I need confirmation of the intended boundary and whether another engine source copy or helper owns this logic.
